$comment: Baseline for `pnpm rls:bypass-check` (scripts/check-tenant-bypass.ts).
This is a RATCHET, not a mute button. The gate is red when a key is missing
here (a new bypass), red when a key's count goes UP (a new call site on an
already-known file), and red when a count goes DOWN (an entry someone fixed
and forgot to remove). Only an exact match is green. `--prune` lowers the
counts for you when work lands; nothing lowers them silently.
kind = 'allowed'  the call site is correct as written and is expected to stay.
kind = 'debt'     the call site is wrong; `card` names who closes it. The gate
prints the outstanding debt on every run, green or red, so a
deferred finding cannot go quiet the way the ones in
TASK-MTSHUZUMVLTBF did.
Measured on 2026-09-10 against dev @ c3c8e9c by TASK-MTVRAZSUVLL9R.
Every 'allowed' reason below was read out of the file it names, not inferred
from the path. See docs/agent-results/TASK-MTVRAZSUVLL9R-de-fb.md §3.
Every `debt` entry has a real card on the board, opened by TASK-MTVRAZSUVLL9R:
TASK-MTVTMZXYT84RZ  wrap the two scopable billing calls (K1)
TASK-MTVTQTJIQ5SDB  MarketplaceListing: catalogue or tenant data? (K3)
TASK-MTVTRNORO1ES8  fabricated tenant ids: esr-parser, storefront (K4+K5)
TASK-MTVSBEO7VX6Y4  the surviving subscription-sync fallback (that card owns the file)
The 35 `allowed` entries are NOT fabrika_app-ready — they are correct as
tenant scoping and return zero rows under a NOBYPASSRLS role. Slice 6,
TASK-MTVTPVTEBCF5Z, gives them a sanctioned cross-tenant path.

entries.subject: apiKey.findUnique
entries.reason: The SHA-256 key hash IS the credential and this lookup is what DISCOVERS the tenant. There is no tenant to scope to until the row comes back, so withTenant cannot wrap it — the argument it needs is this call's result.

entries.subject: applicationPart.findUnique
entries.reason: Magic-token partner portal: there is no session at all. The token is the credential and the row names its own tenant. Same discovery shape as api-auth.ts; the file's own header points at src/modules/m11/server/actions.ts for the reasoning.

entries.subject: applicationPart.findUnique
entries.reason: The comment on the line says it: 'Resolved by token, then re-scoped to that row's own tenant for the write.' The read discovers the tenant; the write that follows is scoped.

entries.subject: membership.findFirst
entries.reason: Answers 'which tenant does this signed-in user own?'. Scoped by session.user.id and role; the tenantId it returns is what createPortalSession is then given.

entries.subject: membership.findMany
entries.reason: GDPR Art. 15/20 portability export, scoped by userId across every tenant the data subject belongs to. A single tenant scope would silently under-deliver the export.

entries.subject: evaluation.findMany
entries.reason: Same export, where: { userId }. The subject's own rows, wherever they live.

entries.subject: effort.findMany
entries.reason: Same export, where: { userId, deletedAt: null } — soft-deleted rows are deliberately excluded so the file cannot resurrect data already asked to be erased.

entries.subject: aiUsageLog.findMany
entries.reason: Same export, where: { userId }.

entries.subject: approvalRequest.findMany
entries.reason: Same export, where: { OR: [{ requesterId }, { approverId }] } — both sides are the subject.

entries.subject: opportunity.findMany
entries.reason: Same export, where: { ownerId: userId }. The file's comment is explicit that it is scoped by ownerId and never by tenantId, because the rest of a tenant's pipeline is not this subject's personal data.

entries.subject: membership.count
entries.reason: GDPR Art. 17: warns when the subject is the last TENANT_OWNER. The question is per-tenant but asked for every tenant the subject is in, so it cannot sit inside one scope.

entries.subject: membership.findMany
entries.reason: Cancels a pending deletion; lists the subject's tenants to revalidate them. where: { userId }.

entries.subject: aiUsageLog.updateMany
entries.reason: Erasure sweep after the grace period: detaches the subject from every tenant at once, where: { userId }. Wrapping it per tenant would mean enumerating tenants from the row set it is about to change.

entries.subject: effort.deleteMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep, where: { userId }.

entries.subject: calendarConnection.deleteMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep, where: { userId }. Calendar tokens are the subject's own credentials.

entries.subject: savedSearch.deleteMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep, where: { userId }.

entries.subject: opportunity.updateMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep: nulls ownerId so the tenant keeps its pipeline while the subject is detached.

entries.subject: feedback.updateMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep: nulls userId on the subject's feedback rows.

entries.subject: proposalUsage.updateMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep: nulls usedByUserId.

entries.subject: relationship.updateMany
entries.reason: Same erasure sweep: nulls ownerUserId.

entries.subject: feedback.findMany
entries.reason: Platform admins triage across tenants. The file states it and the route is gated by the admin layout; each action re-checks the role with requirePlatformAdmin().

entries.subject: feedback.update
entries.reason: The triage write behind requirePlatformAdmin(). Updates one row by id in whichever tenant raised it.

entries.subject: moduleState.findMany
entries.reason: The module console renders a tenant x module grid; the read is unfiltered on purpose and the page groups by s.tenantId afterwards.

entries.subject: moduleState.findMany
entries.reason: Behind requirePlatformAdmin(); reads one named tenant's states (where: { tenantId }) to evaluate the dependency graph before flipping a module. Wrappable in principle — kept with its sibling read on the same console rather than split across two access styles; see the proposed card K-2.

entries.subject: subscription.groupBy
entries.reason: 'How many live subscriptions does each plan have' is a cross-tenant count by definition; it feeds the platform plan console.

entries.subject: subscription.count
entries.reason: computePublishImpact and countLiveSubscriptions: how many tenants a plan change would touch. Both are questions about the whole estate.

entries.subject: feedback.findMany
entries.reason: The function's own docstring: 'Reads the window and everything still open, both cross-tenant.' It builds the platform's beta digest, not a tenant's.

entries.subject: relationship.findMany
entries.reason: Cron fan-out: reads every tenant's due relationship actions, then groups by focal point. The tenant set is the query's OUTPUT, so no single scope exists to run it in.

entries.subject: savedSearch.findMany
entries.reason: Same fan-out shape: the daily job reads every tenant's alert-enabled saved searches before mailing each one.

entries.subject: lifetimeLicence.findFirst
entries.reason: Two genuinely global reads: the highest `seq` across the whole estate (the licence number is a platform-wide scarce resource, capped at LIFETIME_LICENCE_CAP), and findRecorded(), the idempotency lookup by providerEventId — which runs BEFORE the tenant is known, exactly like api-auth.ts.

entries.subject: subscription.findUnique
entries.reason: tenantId is already a parameter of this function — nothing discovers it, nothing aggregates. This is a plain unwrapped tenant read that slices 1-4 did not reach because src/lib/billing/** was fenced off for another card.

entries.subject: lifetimeLicence.create
entries.reason: Writes data: { tenantId, ... } with the tenant in hand. Unlike its two findFirst siblings in the same file this one is scopable, and under fabrika_app an unscoped INSERT is REFUSED by the WITH CHECK clause — a paid lifetime licence would fail to record.

entries.subject: marketplaceListing.findMany
entries.reason: The line's comment calls MarketplaceListing 'a cross-tenant catalogue by design', but the model carries a non-null tenantId in prisma/schema.prisma and therefore HAS a tenant_isolation policy. Catalogue and policy contradict each other: either the column and policy are wrong, or this read leaks one tenant's listings to another. Unlike Topic and ConceptTemplate this cannot be settled by an exemption — the schema has to decide.

entries.subject: tenantId-collapse-ternary
entries.reason: `...(tenantId ? { tenantId } : {})` on an auditEvent.create DATA object, not a where clause. AuditEvent.tenantId is String? (NULLABLE_TENANT since TASK-MTU6HUB8FUHMG C-2) and a tenant-less subject legitimately writes NULL; the spread omits a column rather than widening a filter. The rule is kept position-blind on purpose — deciding 'is this a where or a data' needs context the scanner does not have, and one documented exemption is cheaper than a rule that guesses.

entries.subject: tenantId-fallback
entries.reason: `tenantId: tenantId ?? 'anonymous'` in a logger.error payload. Not a query, so nothing leaks — but it puts an id in the observability record that matches no Tenant row, which is how the ghost-alert pile in scripts/check-orphan-alerts.ts got started. src/lib/llm.ts already has the right answer for this position: the declared PLATFORM_SCOPE_TENANT_ID, not an ad-hoc word.

entries.subject: tenantId-fallback
entries.reason: `tenantId: (subscription.metadata?.tenantId as string) ?? ''` in a logger.warn payload. The empty string is exactly what assertTenantScope rejects, so the log line names a tenant that can never be looked up. This file had TWO of these when the baseline was written; TASK-MTVSBEO7VX6Y4 removed the second (a `|| ''` in the handler's return value on the already-processed path) while this card was running, and the gate reported the fall as a warning rather than blocking that agent's push. The survivor belongs to the same card.

entries.subject: tenantId-fallback
entries.reason: `tenantId: tenantId || 'system'` is passed to generateText, which writes AiUsageLog.tenantId and charges credits (src/lib/llm.ts:405-424). AiUsageLog IS tenant-scoped, so a fabricated 'system' lands a usage row against a tenant that does not exist. The repo already declares the correct value for this case — PLATFORM_SCOPE_TENANT_ID ('__platform__'), whose docstring says in as many words that it is 'a declared scope, not a stand-in for a tenant we failed to look up' and that its underscore form cannot collide with a cuid or slug. 'system' can.
